definition: A device with two coils of insulated wire on a soft-iron core that changes the size of an alternating voltage; it works only with a.c.
The input coil of a transformer, connected to the a.c. supply.
The output coil of a transformer, in which an alternating e.m.f. is induced and from which the output is taken.
A transformer with more turns on the secondary coil than on the primary coil, so the output voltage is bigger than the input voltage.
A transformer with fewer turns on the secondary coil than on the primary coil, so the output voltage is smaller than the input voltage.
